logic: Each case states database rows as in sync/admin-manifest.json (input: now, donors, payments, donations and, where the computation reads them, links and symbolClaims) and, in input.chunks, the rows of every chunk of the administration's device copy the computation reads, keyed <part>/<chunk id> as the device stores them (donations/payments:<yyyy-mm>, donations/donations:<yyyy-mm>, donations/donor-records:<yyyy-mm>, donations/links:<yyyy-mm>, donations/symbol-claims, donations/receipts:<year>, donors/accounts:<yyyy-mm>), with ids aliased as CaseRows names them. The backend runner writes the rows, checks that the sync endpoints answer exactly input.chunks (and input.summary where given), then asks the endpoint for every query of input.queries; the browser runner computes each answer from input.chunks alone. Both compare the whole list of answers with expected.answers. The computation is the account list of /sprava/darci, GET /api/admin/donors?query=&page=&limit= (limit 20 by default): every account, erased ones and administrators included, whose name or e-mail, with the Czech accented letters folded and lowercased, contains the trimmed query folded the same way, or whose variable symbol starts with it (a blank query finds every account), ordered by name and then e-mail, the page-th page of limit accounts, each the account row of the copy as it is, and hasMore when an account follows the page. Names and e-mails are ordered by their Unicode code points, as the database collation of the server's PostgreSQL image (en_US.utf8 on musl) compares them byte by byte, so lower-case and accented initials come after Z.

cases.name: Accounts found by name or e-mail without accents or by the start of the symbol, erased ones too, by name then e-mail, a page at a time
Names ordered by their characters' code points as the database collation orders them, lower-case and accented initials after Z, a page at a time
A character beyond the Basic Multilingual Plane orders by its code point, after the full-width letters, as the database orders its bytes
